The incidence of cancer in dogs is significantly elevated compared to humans—lymphoma occurs 2~5 times more often, mammary cancer 4 times, osteosarcoma 8 times, and skin cancer 35 times more frequently in dogs. For dogs aged 8 and older, the cancer incidence rate approaches 40~50%. Despite the growing market for pet medications, the development of new veterinary drugs has not kept pace with demand. Existing pet immuno-oncology drugs are primarily repurposed from human treatments, which often leads to lower efficacy and concerns about side effects when used in animals. In response to this market demand, Vaxcellbio has developed VCB-2401(Vaxleukin-15), an immuno-oncology drug specifically for pets. Pet Cancer Drug Market VCB-2401
